title: ADVANCED SUSTAINABLE MANUFACTURING OF SPACE-QUALIFIED COMPONENTS FROM RECYCLED HIGH-VALUE FEEDSTOCK - EXPRO+
description: Objective:To identify, demonstrate, and implement recycling of high-value scrap into quality feedstock for additivemanufacturing of components for space applications.Description:As the demand for spacecraft, satellites and launch systems grows, so too does the consumption of criticalraw materials - many of which are finite, expensive and environmentally burdensome to extract. Recycling andreusing materials offer a strategic solution, reducing dependency on virgin resources, lowering carbonemissions and enhancing supply chain resilience. By integrating recycled materials into components, thespace sector can not only reduce its environmental footprint but also pioneer circular economy practices that will be essential for long-term sustainability - both on Earth and in future off-world manufacturing ecosystems.Furthermore, materials like titanium, aluminium and nickel alloys are in high demand in the space sector, yetthese materials are primarily imported from non-European sources. Developing local recycling solutions for high-value, critical materials is a vital step towards achieving European material self-sufficiency, especially in the current geopolitical and economic context. Potentially significant sources of scrap include machining waste (e.g. swarf, off cuts) and unused powder from additive manufacturing. Scrapped parts due to manufacturing defects are expected to be a secondary, less frequent, source but may become more relevant in the context of out-of-earth manufacturing. The space sector should also consider sourcing waste/scrap materials from other industries (e.g. aviation, automotive).The activity will start by identifying hot spots of high-value material scrap across European manufacturing(space and non-space). A hot spot in this context would be defined as materials with high volume of scrap,high material value/cost, raw material being sourced outside Europe, and high demand by the space industry.Selected scrap will then be processed into quality raw materials, tested, and used to produce and evaluate ademonstrator part to be defined based on a business case (e.g. bracket, fuel tank).This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Identify sources of scrap material, material types relevant for space, and their possible use; down-selection of the most interesting cases (including economic, ecological and technical factors).- Develop processing route(s) for high-value material waste identified in the first task to transform into highquality raw materials for use as space hardware. This will most likely require dedicated alloy development to factor in what properties and quality can be realistically extracted from recycled materials.- Develop the advanced manufacturing process(es) for the use of "up-cycled" materials, considering theinfluence of impurities, potential development of detrimental phases, etc.- Test the produced material on a sample level (material characteristics, mechanical properties, etc.).- Design and manufacture a relevant spacedemonstrator part for subsequent testing to check compliance with relevant functional requirements.- Provide guidance on how to design components produced from recycled materials, seeking to identifypotential trade-offs between quality requirements, safety factors, cost and lead time.Deliverables: Breadboard, Report

title: HIGH PERFORMANCE INSULATING MATERIALS FOR L4 ENCELADUS LANDER - EXPRO+
description: To assess the potential use of alternative insulating materials (e.g. aerogel) to improve the thermal performance of classical MLI,and sustaining the extreme environments applicable to L4 Enceladus Lander.Current thermal insulation solutions for Solar System missions are mainly based onconductive and radiative insulation (e.g. JUICE Nomex reinforced MLI), or includeconvective insulation function, not assessed for L4 Enceladus Lander environments (e.g.ExoMars Upilex foam). Due to the L4 Lander extreme environment on Enceladus (lowtemperatures, potential interaction with plumes, snow and/or ice and challenging landingconditions), the use of classical MLI technology, even with an efficient, reinforced designsuch as the one used in JUICE, is probably insufficient to achieve the required thermalinsulation and reduce the use of electrical heating. Heaters use is to be minimized (with atarget of 0 W), as the electrical power consumption is directly linked to the mass andlifetime span of the Lander on Enceladus surface. In addition, the selected thermal controltechnologies shall ensure nominal performance while keeping physical integrity (stringentmechanical loads during landing) and fulfilling mass, EMC, planetary protection and otherrequirements of the mission.Potential technologies such as Aerogel have been identified in similar missions such asMars Pathfinder ("(...). The WEB is a thermal isolating composite structure with cocuredthermal control surfaces and an ultralightweight hydrophobic solid silica aerogel whichminimizes conduction and radiation. This design provides excellent thermal insulation atlow gas pressures and meets the structural requirements for spacecraftlaunch loads andfor a 60 g impact landing at Mars without damage to the insulation or structure. (...)",https://www.jstor.org/stable/44725574). The use of these technologies or alternative onesneeds being assessed for L4 Enceladus Lander. The activity encompasses the followingtasks:Requirements consolidation and assessment of state of the art- Design of breadboard and associated test bench- Manufacture of breadboard, test bench- Execution of tests and exploitation of results- Conclusions elaboration and roadmap for further development towards a flight applicationThe outcomes of this activity are extendable to other planetary missions.

title: DETERMINISTIC ETHERNET SPACE TIME-SENSITIVE NETWORKING SOFT IP CORE - EXPRO+
description: Objective:To develop a technology independent soft IP (Intellectual Property) core that complies with the aerospace profile of TSN(Time Sensitive Networking).Description:TSN (Time-Sensitive Networking) and TTE (Time Triggered Ethernet) are the two technologies that allow to deliver determinism and quality of service on top of standard Ethernet networks. Since TTE can be considered  relatively closed technology (i.e. proprietary solution, patents pending on the technology), since a few years TSN is emerging as a potential successor of that technology. TSN is IEEE supported set of standards that implements wide range of quality of services (i.e. reliability, determinism, mixed criticality traffic, redundancy, time synchronization) on top of the standard Ethernet protocols. TSN benefits from Ethernet Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) tools/ecosystem, it is free of patents and is being introduced step-by step in industrial applications (automotive/industrial) and aerospace domain (IEEE P802.1DP - TSN for Aerospace Onboard Ethernet Communications). Although TSN is very successful in the automotive/industrial sector, in space applications TSNis still being considered as low TRL technology. Many current and future Exploration and Space Transportationmissions are considering Ethernet-based networks for the data-handling communication bus. Having thistechnology available for future ESA missions is seen as a key driver for future missions. The aim of this activity Is to develop an IP core that contains the core functionalities of Time-Sensitive Networking needed for space applications. Although the set of TSN standards is very wide, there are several on-going activities aiming attailoring of TSN for space applications. Having an TSN IP tailored to space applications could be considered asa key enabler of this technology in future ESA and national missions.The following technical aspects shall be considered:- Development of End-system IP Core. Switch IP core is out of scope of this activity- One or two Ethernet ports shall be supported.- Host integration: AXI4 lite for registers and IP configuration, and AXI4 stream for packet data- The IP shall support 10/100/1000Mbps speeds. 10Gbps is considered optional.- Compatible and configurable with various PHY interfaces (i.e. MII/GMII/RGMIII).- To be developed as technology independent VHDL.- To be implemented and validated in 2 FPGA/ASIC technologies (preferable NG-Ultra/Ultra300 andMicrochip Polarfire).This activity encompasses the following tasks:- TSN IP core requirements identification and development of the high-level architecture of the TSN soft IP core.- Prototype development and integration into a representative Field-Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) based network platform.- Verification and validation targeting high speed use cases- TSN soft IP core release and related documentation.Deliverables: Prototype, Report, SoftwareApplication/Need Date: Exploration and Space Transportation missions. Mission Classification: alpha, beta,gamma, delta

title: HE-SWE-03B - GLOBAL MULTI-MOMENT MULTI-FLUID MODEL OF THE MAGNETOSPHERE
description: The Agency seeks to assess the applicability and operational potential of a multi-moment, multi-fluid modelling approach for forecasting and nowcasting the Earth's magnetospheric space weather environment. While current operational systems predominantly rely on global MHD models and fully kinetic approaches remain computationally challenging for routine use, this activity aims to demonstrate whether a multi-fluid framework can provide an effective balance between physical realism and operational performance. Bidders are expected to employ real observational data for model verification, validation, calibration, and performance enhancement, investigating techniques such as data assimilation, data-driven boundary conditions, and other observation-informed methods to improve forecasting capability and scientific fidelity. The activity should include comprehensive testing against measurements and reference models, the assessment of computational performance and operational suitability, and the quantification of forecasting skill for key space weather phenomena. The work shall identify the strengths, limitations, and maturity of the approach, while establishing a clear roadmap towards a future three-dimensional global magnetospheric forecasting capability that can operate faster than real time and support advanced operational space weather services.

title: S3-CL-05 SIMPLIFIED LCA AND ECODESIGN TOOL FOR SPACE MISSIONS - EXPRO+
description: Following the endorsement of the ESA Ecodesign Policy in October 2025, the systematic integration of ecodesign principles into ESA programmes and projects has become a key enabler for achieving ESA Green Agenda objectives. However, current Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) approaches remain too complex and resource-intensive for routine use during mission conception and preliminary design. This activity addresses this gap through the development of a simplified LCA and ecodesign tool for space missions, enabling rapid environmental assessments and the comparison of alternative design solutions during phases A/B1. The tool developed in this activity will provide a practical and harmonised means to support ecodesign implementation across the European space sector while ensuring consistency with ESA environmental datasets and European assessment methodologies. The project targets bringing the technology to TRL 6.

title: S3-CL-16 ROBOTICS CUBESAT DEMONSTRATOR MISSION STUDY AND PAYLOAD MATURATION EXPRO+
description: Robotics technologies are fundamental enablers for future In-Orbit Servicing missions. This activity aims to mature a generic robotic actuator integrating position and force sensing, active compliance and variable impedance control towards an in-orbit demonstration mission. The activity will consolidate the mission architecture and payload design, develop a Proto Flight Model, and mature the technology to TRL7 while advancing the overall demonstration mission towards implementation. The resulting mission will validate keyrobotic capabilities required for future servicing, docking and manipulation operations in orbit.
